description: We’re two college freshmen combining software development and computer engineering with one shared ambition: build something that matters. We’re early in our journey, but we’re ready to take on big challenges, learn fast, and turn bold ideas into working solutions. NASA Space Apps is our chance to put that mindset into action - bringing curiosity, creativity, and two different engineering perspectives to problems bigger than ourselves.
summary: After each decision, the base reacts and the game explains what changed. Players can compare the two plans from the same starting reserves, then review their decisions in a final debrief. For example, expanding the greenhouse uses power now and provides food later. NASA resources on deep-space habitation and crop research informed the scenarios. The game uses fictional values and compressed timelines to make these engineering trade-offs easier to understand.
details: Moonbase Five is a 2D browser game that helps students explore the decisions involved in running a Moon base. Players guide astronaut Astra through five stations covering power, food production, radiation shelter, water recycling, and a final science survey. At each station, they choose between two plans. The mission is complete if energy, life support, and food all stay above zero through the fifth decision. Science points track research separately. The base visibly reacts to each decision. Players can compare both plans from the same starting reserves while keeping their original choice. Some decisions carry forward. Expanding greenhouse lighting uses power now and adds food after a time jump. Choosing a protected work bay reduces the life-support cost of a later survey. The final debrief shows the full decision trail and invites players to explain what they would change on another run. The intended benefit is to help students explain why a decision that helps one system can strain another. We designed for beginners by showing plan costs up front, offering an optional hint at the first station, and letting players reach each station with one click. NASA resources on deep-space habitation, crop growth, and greenhouse design informed the scenarios. Resource points, timelines, and system effects are fictional teaching choices. Automated tests covered all 32 choice paths. Student learning outcomes have yet to be evaluated. The game was built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Canvas. It runs offline in a browser with no special hardware. OpenAI Codex assisted with the code, writing, visual design, testing, and demo slides. The prototype was developed before the November 14–15, 2026 hackathon.
